Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

organise verb

put in order, plan out (things, one’s time)

also organize, put in order, plan out, organised, well organised

classical

Plin. Ep. 9.36.1: quemadmodum in Tuscīs diem aestāte dispōnam

dispōnō, dispōnere, disposuī, dispositum

verb, third conjugation, transitive

arrange, organise, lay out

Lewis & Short: “to place here and there, to set in different places, to distribute regularly, to dispose, arrange”. An orderly life is vīta disposita (Plin. Ep. 3.1.2).

Other words

  • ōrdinō, ōrdināre, ōrdināvī, ōrdinātum — put in order, arrange

    verb, first conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Nep. Iph. 2.2; Liv. 29.1 (Lewis & Short)

    Lewis & Short: “to order, set in order, arrange, adjust, dispose, regulate”. The household word for tidying (see tidy up).

  • dīgerō, dīgerere, dīgessī, dīgestum — sort out, set in order (papers, the calendar)

    verb, third conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Ov. F. 1.27: tempora dīgereret cum conditor urbis

    See sort.

Examples

  • quaeris, quemadmodum in Tuscīs diem aestāte dispōnam

    You ask how I organise my day in summer at my Tuscan villa.Plin. Ep. 9.36.1

  • mē autem ut certus sīderum cursus ita vīta hominum disposita dēlectat

    As the sure course of the stars delights me, so does an orderly life.Plin. Ep. 3.1.2

  • nihil esse pulchrius in omnī ratiōne vītae dispositiōne atque ōrdine

    Nothing in any walk of life is finer than arrangement and order.Col. 12.2.4

See also tidy up, sort, set out, order, organise.
